items.title: Moderna stock nearly doubles as Merck-partnered mRNA cancer vaccine meets Phase 3 goal
items.snippet: Melanoma was slower to recur in patients receiving Merck and Moderna's mRNA vaccine with Keytruda, supporting use of the combination in adjuvant treatment. The partners plan to take the data to the FDA.

items.title: Trump picks White House aide Heidi Overton as FDA chief: reports
items.snippet: If Heidi Overton clears the Senate nomination process, analysts say she will have a tough job ahead to “restore predictability” to an agency battered by layoffs and controversial policies.

items.title: Enveda’s exercise-simulating obesity tablet clears early clinical test
items.snippet: Touting an “exceptional” gastrointestinal safety profile for its oral obesity drug candidate in a study of healthy volunteers, Enveda plans to test the asset in people stopping GLP-1 treatment.

items.title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
items.snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

items.title: Amylyx’s redemption story, Summit’s survival woes, Definium’s anxiety win, more
items.snippet: Amylyx shares good news for its investigational GLP-1 blocker; Definium announces positive data for its LSD-based therapy in anxiety; Summit/Akeso’s ivonescimab shows degrading survival benefits; patients treated with Neurocrine’s Prader-Willi drug experience serious adverse events; and Eli Lilly cracks down on the bl...

items.title: Leadership Lab: The one person executives need by their side
items.snippet: An executive who is rarely short on ideas needs someone to pull their big ideas through to implementation. Kaye/Bassman’s Michael Pietrack explains why this person, who he calls the implementer, may be the most important hire in the building.

items.title: Takeda leads wave of orexin drugs with potential to upend narcolepsy market
items.snippet: The FDA’s August approval of Takeda’s Orzeyful for treating the full set of narcolepsy symptoms initiated a new era in the sleep market.

items.title: With China rising, Hong Kong builds bridge to biotech innovation
items.snippet: Massachusetts-based biotech accelerator LabCentral signed an agreement with Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks Corporation in June to connect founders with the U.S. ecosystem—and fuel more innovation.

items.title: Novo takes first round of oral obesity duel. Can it stay ahead of Lilly?
items.snippet: Despite coming away with an early victory over Eli Lilly in the oral obesity face-off, analysts don’t expect Novo Nordisk’s lead to last for very long.

items.title: EMD Serono cuts 20 at Massachusetts research site
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: Sandoz inks $322M Henlius deal for rights to as many as 10 biosimilars
items.snippet: The initial batch of biosimilars includes copies of Amgen, Eli Lilly and GSK drugs that collectively generate billions of dollars in annual revenues.

items.title: LEO adds to dermatology portfolio with $435M deal for late-stage rare disease drug
items.snippet: This is the third recent acquisition conducted by Denmark’s LEO Pharma in medical dermatology, a portfolio that marked 12% growth in the first half of the year.

items.title: Rebounding biotech funds expected to spur CDMO growth within year
items.snippet: With demand for pharma services historically lagging changes in biotech funding, analysts expect CDMOs to experience an uptick in activity in late 2026 or early 2027.

items.title: Regeneron ends eye disease study due to antibody's safety profile
items.snippet: The discontinuation of the uveitis study adds to Regeneron’s series of clinical setbacks, including the Phase 3 failures of the Dupixent follow-up itepekimab and an investigational combo regimen for melanoma.

items.title: Amylyx eyes FDA filing for GLP-1 blocker after late-stage win in post-bariatric hypoglycemia
items.snippet: With a Phase 3 trial showing a reduction of serious and severe hypoglycemic episodes in patients who have undergone weight loss surgery, Amylyx Pharmaceuticals plans to file for approval this year. If granted market entry, avexitide could hit peak sales of $1.7 billion worldwide, analysts estimate.

items.title: Assessing shared failures with AI is key to cell and gene therapy’s evolution
items.snippet: If we guard our secrets, patients suffer. Only through a commitment to transparency and data sharing—and artificial intelligence—can we make cell and gene therapies safer and more effective.

items.title: EyePoint’s Phase 3 fail sends stock spiraling amid next-gen AMD race
items.snippet: EyePoint’s quest to reduce treatment burden for patients with age-related macular degeneration has hit a bump in the road, with a clinical miss driving the biotech’s stock down by 70%.

items.title: Summit, Akeso’s China approval celebration cut short as survival benefit degrades
items.snippet: Ivonescimab notched its third approval in China last week, but the label update has tempered expectations for the Summit Therapeutics/Akeso drug, showing that progression-free survival declines over time.

items.title: AstraZeneca pulls plug on late-stage lung cancer trial, taking another clinical blow
items.snippet: AstraZeneca will push through with its other Phase 3 studies for volrustomig, including in cervical cancer and mesothelioma.

items.title: Vera’s newly approved IgA nephropathy drug supports kidney function, like Otsuka’s Voyxact
items.snippet: Otsuka Pharmaceuticals’ Voyxact is not the only IgA nephropathy drug that can slow the decline of kidney function. Vera Therapeutics’ Trutakna, which the FDA granted accelerated approval last month, showed “impressive” stabilization, analysts say.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

items.title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
items.snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.

items.title: BIO 2026: Cell and gene therapy sector must break the mold to thrive
items.snippet: If cell and gene therapy makers are going to achieve their mission to improve patients’ lives, the industry must come together to share information across stakeholders, from regulators to manufacturers to payers.

items.title: At FDA, ‘caretaker mode’ is better than power trip mode
items.snippet: UniQure’s planned third-quarter submission for its Huntington’s disease gene therapy may be a harbinger of a more flexible FDA under acting commissioner Kyle Diamantas—but how long will it last? And how can companies be sure these positive decisions won’t just be reversed?
